kept.excerpt: Tucker Carlson branded President Donald Trump a “weak” man who allowed Israel to strong-arm him into the Iran war. The remarks came during a July 15 interview on Bloomberg journalist Mishal Husain’s podcast. Carlson said, “I have held him directly accountable, it’s his fault, he’s the U.S. president, he was elected.”
kept.relevance: This recent public criticism establishes a potential trigger for a retaliatory personal attack by Trump before the deadline.

kept.excerpt: Carlson said he had not spoken to Trump since the regime-change war began and added, “I’m not interested in talking to him.” He said, “I’m going to help build a third party,” while also stating that he was not a politician or a rival to Trump for power.
kept.relevance: This firsthand interview documents the breakdown in their relationship and Carlson’s proposed political activity as possible sources of further conflict.

kept.excerpt: Carlson told Sky News interviewer Yalda Hakim that his last conversation with Trump was February 27, before the Iran war began. In a separate interview with Jack Neel, Carlson mocked Trump’s posture toward Iran and said, “Shut up, b*tch! I don’t take you seriously.” The article also reported that Trump had called Carlson a “low-IQ person” and “highly overrated” in a Truth Social post.
kept.relevance: This report documents continuing public hostility and an absence of direct communication, while corroborating earlier personal insults from Trump.

kept.excerpt: Carlson said on the podcast “Can’t Be Censored” that “there’s no chance I would support the Republican Party” ahead of the November midterm elections. He also said he would not support the Democratic Party. The Associated Press reported that his estrangement from Republicans had intensified after Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran.
kept.relevance: Carlson’s public withdrawal of support from Trump’s party provides additional context for the feud and potential further attacks.

kept.excerpt: Trump wrote, “It’s easy! Tucker is a Low IQ person - Always easy to beat, and highly overrated!!!” The April 17 Truth Social compilation records the statement at 5:12 a.m. Pacific time.
kept.publisher: Donald Trump, Truth Social; archived by The American Presidency Project
kept.relevance: This dated public statement supplies a direct precedent for personal and professional insults against Carlson, subject to whether it falls after the unspecified market creation date.

kept.excerpt: Trump opened a Truth Social post with, “Who’s dumber, Tucker Carlson or Joe Kent?” He later wrote, “Kent is a LOSER, just like Tucker, Candace, Megyn, and the rest of them are LOSERS,” and described them as “LOW IQ.” The compilation records the post at 3:08 p.m. Pacific time on April 16.
kept.publisher: Donald Trump, Truth Social; archived by The American Presidency Project
kept.relevance: The statement provides another direct example of the derogatory personal language specified in the resolution rules, with eligibility dependent on the market creation date.

kept.excerpt: ABC News reported that Trump posted a lengthy critique of Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly, Candace Owens and Alex Jones on Truth Social. Trump said they had “one thing in common, Low IQs” and wrote, “They’re not ‘MAGA,’ they’re losers.” The article was published April 9, 2026, at 9:42 p.m. ET.
kept.relevance: Contemporaneous national news coverage independently corroborates Trump’s use of personal insults against Carlson rather than policy disagreement alone.
